attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person words in his own Substack post, reporting his own test of Imagen 4.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: 'far better in some ways, especially text' and '0 for 4' on horse-riding-astronaut. Correctly treated as a report of his own sample, not a claim the scene is impossible.

contract.note: Taking the 2022 Imagen as baseline follows from the surrounding text. Limiting the claim to his four outputs is a fair, ordinary plain reading. Requiring independent inspection of those outputs is reasonable.

evidence.note: Google's own June 24, 2025 claim of better text rendering than its prior models (Imagen 3). This is a company disclosure, not an independent comparison against the 2022 baseline, and it says nothing about the four horse images.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet independently checks the four reported outputs. The only text-rendering evidence is Google's own claim, made against a different baseline. Neither part of the claim is established or refuted by the evidence the contract requires.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'text in general better' with the 'not in this image' caveat, and 'remains dreadful' for non-10:10 watch times. The fix narrowing the scope to Imagen 4 is appropriate.

contract.note: Reading 'dreadful' as generally unreliable, not never correct, is an ordinary plain reading. Anchoring the claim to the June 2025 model matches when he wrote it.

evidence.note: A study of non-10:10 clock times across many models, with images generated in October 2026. It falls outside the target period, and the abstract does not single out the June 2025 Imagen 4, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: There is no representative evaluation of the June 2025 Imagen 4 on watch times, and no comparable evaluation of its text rendering. The October 2026 study covers a different period and does not match the model. The evidence does not settle either part.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words describing his own test in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: o3 better on some old examples, and still fails the new woman-and-watch prompt.

contract.note: Reading 'o3' as ChatGPT image generation used through o3 is reasonable, and does not decide the result. Counting any wrong requested detail as a failure fits the plain meaning of 'can't do'.

evidence.note: Independent August 2025 test, but on a different prompt (a 4:30 clock) and a later model (GPT-5). It does not test the woman-and-watch prompt on o3 in June 2025.

reviews.rationale: The only record of the o3 outputs is the speaker's own post, which cannot prove itself. The OfficeChai test involves a different prompt, model and month. Neither part of the claim is independently established or refuted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words reporting his own Imagen 4 output.

semantics.note: 'Still fails' could read as general, but the statement reports one displayed output. The contract properly narrows the claim to that output.

contract.note: The checklist of colours, shapes and stack order follows the prompt he quoted. Scoping the claim to the reported output is a fair plain reading.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no evidence items. No authenticated copy of the block image, and no independent inspection of it, was found. Marcus's own description cannot prove itself, so the claim is unresolved.
